chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Harun ibn Kharijah, from Abi Basir, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “Were it not that I fear causing hardship for my Ummah, I would have delayed the 'atamah prayer until one-third of the night. And you remain within a concession until half of the night, and that is the deep darkness of the night. So when the deep darkness has passed, two angels call out: whoever slept through the obligatory salat (prayer) after half of the night, may his eyes find no sleep.”

key_terms.الْعَتَمَةَ: the night prayer, referring here to the late evening salat (prayer)
key_terms.رُخْصَةٍ: a concession or allowance in the time of performance
key_terms.غَسَقُ اللَّيْلِ: the deep darkness of the night
key_terms.مَلَكَانِ: two angels who call out after the passing of that time
key_terms.نِصْفِ اللَّيْلِ: half of the night, marking the limit mentioned in the hadith

ai.seo_question: Until when may the night prayer be delayed, and what warning is mentioned for sleeping past it?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم would have preferred delaying the night prayer later were it not for the hardship upon the community. It indicates a concession for performing it until half of the night and strongly warns against sleeping past the prescribed time of the obligatory salat (prayer).
